questions.question: All the living things are composed of which basic units?
questions.explanation: The text states that all living things are composed of cells.

questions.question: The cell is defined as the structural and functional unit of which entity?
questions.explanation: The cell is defined as the structural and functional unit of the living body.

questions.question: Which unit is the smallest that has all the characteristics of life?
questions.explanation: A single cell is the smallest unit that has all the characteristics of life.

questions.question: Which cell is given as an exception to reproduction by division?
questions.explanation: The text states there are exceptions like the neuron which do not reproduce.

questions.question: Each cell produces its own energy necessary for which processes?
questions.explanation: Cells produce energy necessary for their growth, repair, and other activities.

questions.question: Cells show an immediate response to the entry of which substances?
questions.explanation: Cells show immediate response to the entry of invaders like bacteria or toxic substances.

questions.question: Cells maintain the medium for which purpose?
questions.explanation: Cells maintain the medium, the environment, for their survival.

questions.question: A group of cells having similar function is defined as what?
questions.explanation: Tissue is defined as the group of cells having similar function.

questions.question: How many major types of primary tissues exist in the body?
questions.explanation: All tissues are classified into four major types called the primary tissues.

questions.question: Skeletal and smooth are examples of which primary tissue?
questions.explanation: Muscle tissue includes skeletal muscle, smooth muscle, and cardiac muscle.

questions.question: Neurons and supporting cells make up which type of tissue?
questions.explanation: Nervous tissue consists of neurons and supporting cells.

questions.question: Squamous and columnar are types of which tissue?
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue includes squamous, columnar, and cuboidal epithelial cells.

questions.question: Cartilage and bone belong to which primary tissue category?
questions.explanation: Connective tissue includes connective tissue proper, cartilage, bone, and blood.

questions.question: An organ is formed by how many primary tissue types at minimum?
questions.explanation: An organ is formed by two or more primary types of tissues.

questions.question: Organs composed of all four primary tissue types are known as what?
questions.explanation: The text states that some organs are composed of all four types of primary tissues.

questions.question: Compact organs are also known by which term?
questions.explanation: The organs are of two types, namely tubular or hollow organs and compact or parenchymal organs.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an organ in the body?
questions.explanation: The text lists pancreas among organs such as brain, heart, lungs, stomach, intestine, liver, and kidneys.

questions.question: A group of organs working together carries out specific functions of which entity?
questions.explanation: An organ system is defined as a group of organs that work together to carry out specific functions of the body.

questions.question: The digestive system is concerned with which process?
questions.explanation: The digestive system is concerned with digestion of food particles.

questions.question: Which system eliminates unwanted substances?
questions.explanation: The excretory system eliminates unwanted substances.

questions.question: Transport of substances between organs is performed by which system?
questions.explanation: The cardiovascular system is responsible for transport of substances between the organs.

questions.question: The supply of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide is the role of which system?
questions.explanation: The respiratory system is concerned with the supply of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Reproduction of species is the function of which system?
questions.explanation: The reproductive system is involved in the reproduction of species.

questions.question: Growth of the body and maintenance of normal life is regulated by which system?
questions.explanation: The endocrine system is concerned with growth of the body and regulation and maintenance of normal life.

questions.question: Stability and movements of the body are functions of which system?
questions.explanation: The musculoskeletal system is responsible for stability and movements of the body.

questions.question: The cell body is formed along with which covering structure?
questions.explanation: Each cell is formed by a cell body and a membrane covering the cell body called the cell membrane.

questions.question: The cell body has which two main parts?
questions.explanation: The cell body has two parts, namely nucleus and cytoplasm surrounding the nucleus.

questions.question: The structure of the cell is studied under how many headings?
questions.explanation: The structure of the cell is studied under three headings: cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus.

questions.question: Which structure is labeled covering the cell in Figure 1.1?
questions.explanation: Figure 1.1 labels the outer covering of the cell as the cell membrane.

questions.question: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum appears in Figure 1.1 as which structure?
questions.explanation: Figure 1.1 labels the smooth endoplasmic reticulum among the cell organelles.
